chunks: From him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man falls ill and makes a will of manumission or charity, he may revoke what he manumitted and what he gave in charity, and do in it whatever he wishes until he dies, and thus is the principle of the will."
ai.seo_question: Can a person revoke their will of charity or manumission before they die?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the right of revocation (ruju') in a will extends beyond mere property distribution to include acts of worship like manumission and charity, affirming the testator's absolute discretion until death. It underscores the Shia legal view that a will is not a binding contract upon the donor's death but a revocable declaration, allowing for adjustments based on changing circumstances or final wishes.
